job.title: Senior Finance Accountant
job.description:
Senior Financial Accountant
12 month fixed term contract, with genuine scope to convert to a permanent role
Norwest, NSW
Hybrid work arrangement, on site parking available
$130,000 - $150,000 base + Superannuation
 
Job Brief
Our client is looking for a Senior Financial Accountant who has genuinely worked inside acquisition activity before, not just studied it. This is a hands on, technical role acting as the go to person for the finance leadership team, covering everything from pre acquisition considerations through to post completion accounting and integration. It suits someone comfortable in a fast changing, occasionally unstructured environment where priorities can shift week to week.
 
About Our Client
Our client is a large, multi entity business with an active acquisition strategy, expecting to move back into acquisition mode over the coming months. The finance function is lean and technically stretched, and this role exists to give the finance leadership team a technically strong person they can rely on for acquisition accounting, technical accounting questions and broader transformation work as the business continues to grow.
 
Responsibilities
  • Provide technical input across acquisitions, covering both pre completion considerations and post completion accounting, including opening balance sheet adjustments and integration of a newly acquired entity's books
  • Act as a technical sounding board for finance leadership on accounting, tax and treasury matters as they come up
  • Support technical calculations tied to executive and ownership structures, including dividend distribution workpapers
  • Contribute to ongoing transformation and process improvement initiatives across the finance function
  • Apply accounting standards to technical positions independently, with minimal oversight
 
Requirements
  • CA or CPA qualified
  • Genuine exposure to acquisition or M&A accounting, whether gained inside an acquisitive business or
  • advising clients through transactions at a chartered accounting firm
  • Comfortable providing technical guidance across accounting, tax and treasury matters
  • Comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast changing, less structured environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, able to translate technical positions clearly for non technical stakeholders
What's on Offer
A technically rich role with genuine influence, working directly with finance leadership on live acquisition activity. Strong salary band reflecting the technical bar required for the role. Genuine scope to convert to a permanent position. On site parking available.

job.title: Head of Client Partnerships

You've built large revenue portfolios. You've led leaders. You've managed complexity without letting it become chaos.

But you're looking for something bigger than simply hitting a number.

We're partnering with a high-growth Australian business that sits at the intersection of commerce, marketing and customer strategy. In just a few years, it has become a major player in its category and is now focused on its next chapter of growth.

They're looking for a Head of Client Partnerships to lead a significant commercial portfolio, a team of experienced people leaders, and a customer base that includes some of the country's largest organisations.

This is not a role where you'll inherit a perfectly polished machine. The business has scaled quickly. The opportunity now is to bring greater consistency, capability and strategic thinking to a high-performing team while continuing to drive ambitious growth targets.

There are three big pieces to the role:
  • You'll own the operational rhythm of a large and complex commercial portfolio. Hundreds of customer opportunities move through the business at any given time. You'll create visibility, discipline and predictability, ensuring the right priorities get attention and leaders stay focused on what matters most. 
  • Second, you'll develop a group of people leaders who are talented, capable and still growing as managers. You'll coach them on performance management, feedback, accountability and leadership fundamentals. That means understanding the customer's broader objectives, engaging more effectively with marketing and brand stakeholders, and helping teams move from selling products to solving business problems.
The person who succeeds in this role will be equally comfortable discussing commercial performance, customer strategy, organisational capability and leadership development.

You'll work for a highly respected executive who is known for setting high standards, backing talented people and developing future leaders.
The culture is ambitious, fast-moving and direct.

People who thrive here are naturally curious, commercially sharp and energised by building things. They're accountable, action-oriented and comfortable operating at pace. They don't wait for someone else to solve a problem.

Importantly, this business offers genuine career opportunity. It has ambitious growth plans, significant investment behind it and a track record of promoting strong performers into broader leadership roles.

You'll likely bring:
  • Experience leading leaders, not just individual contributors.
  • Ownership of a significant commercial portfolio, P&L, client book or customer business.

Background is less important than capability.

You might come from FMCG, media, retail, technology, marketplaces, e-commerce or another customer-led commercial environment.

What matters most is your ability to lead through complexity, create momentum and help a business move from good to great.

job.title: Group FP&A Lead
job.description:
The business

Large-scale infrastructure development. Multiple assets under construction, global institutional backing, and a lot of capital going out the door.
The economics are what make it interesting. Big upfront spend, long-dated contracted revenue, and a lag before asset earnings. There's no long history to extrapolate from and no settled view of unit economics yet. Someone has to build that view and then defend it to investors, lenders and the board.

The role

You'll own the budget and forecast cycle, help build the model that links the construction program to the financial outcome, and produce the reporting the executive actually runs the business off.

The first year is mostly building:
  • The group planning model from scratch. Capex phasing, funding drawdown, the ramp from an asset going live to full contribution
  • A budget and reforecast cycle that gets better each time it runs
  • The metrics that define performance here, and executive agreement on them
  • A planning tool. Right now it's spreadsheets, and that won't hold
  • Board and investor reporting that stands up to institutional scrutiny
Who it suits

There are two routes in, and we're open on both.
You might come from a scale-up, where you built the reporting function yourself and worked without much precedent. The thing to be honest with yourself about is the balance sheet. This business carries a very large asset base and revenue turns up after the spend.

Or from infrastructure, energy, resources or transport, where you've modelled projects from investment decision through construction to revenue. Then the question is pace. There's no process to inherit here and no team of analysts (yet), and decisions happen faster than they do inside a large corporate.

Either works. What matters more is whether you've built something before. If your best work has been running a well-oiled cycle someone else designed, this will frustrate you.

What you'll bring
  • CA, CPA or CFA, or the equivalent in experience
  • Evidence you've built FP&A capability rather than maintained it. What you inherited, what you built, what changed
  • Driver-based modelling across capex, funding and long-dated revenue, not just P&L
  • You've implemented or rebuilt a planning tool
  • The confidence to bring a view to an executive team, not just a number
Apply here with your CV, or email Kunal Gupta at [axr] Recruitment & Search to learn more - kunalg@axr.com.au.

job.title: Regional Sales Manager
job.description:
This is not your standard Regional Sales Manager role.
  
This role is as much about the adventure as it is the career opportunity.
  
It’s the chance to live and work in Papua New Guinea, experience a uniquely fascinating culture and commercial environment and make a genuine impact in one of the country’s most established businesses.
  
Based in Lae, you’ll lead Pacific Industries’ second-largest sales region, build the capability of a sizeable field team and play an important role in the continued growth of the business.
  
Pacific Industries is one of Papua New Guinea’s most established food and beverage businesses and the exclusive PepsiCo bottler in the country. The business grew 70% in FY25 and is up a further 20–25% this year, with a portfolio spanning Pepsi, Mountain Dew, 7UP, Mirinda and Pepsi Max alongside its own iconic local brands.
  
The right person won’t see relocating to Papua New Guinea as simply part of the job. It will be part of the reason they want it.
  
Additional benefits include fully furnished secure accommodation, a company 4WD for business and personal use, an annual return flight to Australia and yacht club membership.
  
What you’ll do

Based in Lae and reporting to the National Sales Manager, you’ll lead the Momase region across Lae, Madang, Wewak and Vanimo, with responsibility for a team of approximately 20–30 sales representatives and merchandisers.
  
This is hands-on commercial leadership, focused on developing the team, improving execution and unlocking the significant growth opportunity that exists across the region.
  
Specific responsibilities include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing the regional sales team
  • Improving trade execution across pricing, planograms, call schedules, share of shelf and in-store standards
  • Building relationships across wholesalers, distributors and independent retailers
  • Using data and commercial insight to identify and unlock growth opportunities
  • Establishing stronger sales reporting, forecasting and performance rhythms
  • Improving debtor management, collections and route-to-market effectiveness
  • Working closely with warehousing and logistics across a complex distribution network
  
You’ll need the following experience and skills
  • Regional or State Sales Management experience within FMCG
  • Experience leading field sales teams across independent, wholesale or distributor channels
  • A track record of coaching people, building capability and managing performance
  • Strong commercial, analytical and customer management skills
  • A solid understanding of trade execution and what great looks like in-store
  • Resilience, adaptability and the ability to operate effectively in a different cultural and commercial environment
  • Most importantly, a genuine commitment to relocating to Lae for at least two years
  
Pacific Industries is looking for someone who can develop capability in others, tell a compelling story through data, persevere when things aren’t straightforward and make the complex simple.
  
About the company

Pacific Industries has been manufacturing and distributing food and beverages in Papua New Guinea since 1936. Today, the third-generation family business employs approximately 800 national staff and 50 expatriates across eleven branches and two manufacturing plants.
  
Since securing the exclusive PepsiCo bottling licence for Papua New Guinea in 2018, the business has entered a significant period of growth and investment, including a new Port Moresby bottling plant commissioned in November 2024.
  
Curious?

If you’re an FMCG sales leader who knows how to build teams, lift execution and grow a region and the idea of doing it in Papua New Guinea excites you, this could be your next great career decision and your next adventure.
  
Start a conversation with Pacific Industries’ chosen recruitment partner for this role, [axr] Recruitment & Search, by hitting the Apply button now.
